and the Gemara answers it is different there because every day becomes purging for its fellow, and he cooked in it peace-offerings of the present or a chatat and afterward peace-offerings — it is hag'alah; and Rashba learns from this why should what one cooks now be hag'alah — it is only ordinary cooking; rather since heter absorbed, even though one cooks heter afterward it weakens its taste and is permitted; but if forbidden matter absorbed, even though its taste is weak, nevertheless there is taste of prohibition in it and it does not help until one hag'alahs it properly — this is his law and proof; and Beit Yosef wrote Tosafot and Rosh challenged how every day becomes purging for its fellow — behold it diminishes through eating and it becomes noten ta'am bar noten ta'am; and they resolved from basar b'chalav that from the Torah it is batel b'rov and in a Temple vessel they establish it on a Torah basis; and therefore Rashba's proof is nothing; and Shach in Netivot HaKesef challenged Beit Yosef and wrote that Tosafot's, Rosh's, and supporters' words do not contradict Rashba — they came only to settle how it is permitted to cook peace-offerings a second time, for it diminishes through eating; and on this they wrote they establish it on a Torah basis and it is batel b'rov, since in the second time there is still no prohibition and it has not yet become notar; and likewise in a chatat that was cooked afterward with peace-offerings for the kohen's portion — they are batel b'rov; but certainly if hag'alah does not help — challenge how one cooks kodashim a third time, since it already became notar; certainly when the vessel became forbidden one cannot say they establish it on a Torah basis and it is batel in the majority, and one cannot say every day becomes purging since it already became forbidden; however it is reasonable to say per Rashba that if heter absorbed hag'alah helps — this, see there where he elaborated; and likewise wrote the responsum of the Gaon R' Gershom in Sefer Avodat HaGershuni see there. And what he elaborated on the body of the matter — if it already became notar one may not rely on bitul b'rov — rather one must understand: Rashba himself compared whether hag'alah helps or not to noten ta'am bar noten ta'am of heter and forbidden matter — for in heter noten ta'am bar noten ta'am is permitted for we are not concerned with weak taste, but in forbidden matter it is forbidden for weak taste also forbids, as Beit Yosef wrote; and therefore Tosafot concluded that regarding chatat it is noten ta'am bar noten ta'am of forbidden matter of chatat forbidden to zarim and the like; if so also for hag'alah it is called forbidden matter; and still difficult: all who cooked chatat in it — how did he cook peace-offerings in it; and Rashba did not hold this reasoning that chatat is called forbidden matter — he did not intend to feed it to zarim, as Shach wrote in Netivot HaKesef; but Tosafot and Rosh who concluded it is called forbidden matter — Rashba's difficulty remains in its place; therefore one must say that certainly through cooking much was expelled from the vessel and the sense of taste will discern when one tastes kafila the taste of absorption will be weak taste, and the taste of the second cooking will absorb in it; and even though chatat meat was absorbed before, nevertheless the majority absorbed is from peace-offerings of the present — a little from yesterday's meat; and therefore absorption inside the vessel is batel b'rov — as we say it is batel inside the cooked dish and as we say it absorbed inside the vessel; and therefore even in chatat and afterward peace-offerings bitul b'rov is possible — not when it already expelled that the law of hag'alah applied, only before chatat meat absorption expelled was in the majority and behold it is like peace-offerings meat — this is Tosafot's intent; and Beit Yosef properly wrote this reasoning of bitul b'rov surrounds everything: in truth in my view Rashba also holds thus — certainly he holds chatatot are called forbidden matter, and it appears from his words in many places in Torat HaBayit and Mishmeret HaBayit; only he holds in a Temple vessel they did not decree because of non-sacred vessels, for in the Temple they separate from non-sacred vessels — what would a non-sacred vessel enter there; also they would have had to fix thus so as not to multiply vessels for kodashim — therefore they establish it on a Torah basis; and these matters are a great difficulty; but kodashim kalim that are eaten anywhere in Jerusalem — every Israelite cooks in his pots as he wishes; if so how is "Temple vessel they establish on a Torah basis" relevant — what does the Temple want here; certainly there is concern because of non-sacred vessels, and a man from his house will not weary to prepare a vessel to cook what happens once a year; and Rashba holds it does not apply to establish on a Torah basis; therefore he properly challenged how cooking helps in place of hag'alah; and on this it answers heter absorbed — these are peace-offerings; but in chatat Rashba concedes forbidden matter absorbed — only here it is a Temple vessel and they establish on a Torah basis, investigate: and therefore Tosafot and Rosh's view that even in peace-offerings they wrote "Temple vessel they establish on a Torah basis" — if so Rashba's words do not exist and Beit Yosef's words are in their place: and one may analyze Rashba — he began this topic to argue in the Gemara that challenges what was taught regarding kodashim they hag'alah in boiling — hag'alah does not help for him, for we learned they whiten in fire; and the Gemara answers every day becomes purging for its fellow — still difficult what of it that purging was done — behold hag'alah does not help; and on this he answered at length — it is satisfactory to answer heter absorbed and forbidden absorbed — where heter absorbed hag'alah helps; and at first glance it still does not settle anything — for if so why did the Gemara need to bring every day becomes purging for its fellow — it should have answered briefly that therefore they hag'alah in boiling and do not whiten, for heter absorbed and boiling suffices without need for all the elaboration; and one must say Rashba holds that when we say heter absorbed, cooking and hag'alah suffice where they hag'alah while still heter, but hag'alah when it already became forbidden does not help and requires libun like forbidden matter; therefore the mishnah that teaches they hag'alah in boiling refers to pouring out and rinsing done when it already became notar and hag'alah does not help; therefore the Gemara answers every day becomes purging, etc. — peace-offerings cooking was done when everything was still heter and notar had not been made; then since the taste of hag'alah weakened in any case it is permitted — and all this if we say pouring out and rinsing was at the time notar was made; but Rambam ruled in chapter 5 of Laws of Sacrificial Procedure law 14 that pouring out and rinsing was done immediately after eating — then the above difficulty is in its place; and necessarily Beit Yosef's answer — Temple vessel is batel b'rov; therefore when they intend to hag'alah it in boiling bitul b'rov does not apply and it is "one may not annul prohibition l'chatchila"; but when they cook in it a second time their intent is for eating and cooking and it is not in the category of "one may not annul prohibition" for what happened incidentally — investigate: and Tosafot supplement Zevachim daf 96 s.v. learn from this — after he answered this difficulty of noten ta'am bar noten ta'am, etc., Temple vessel is batel in the majority — they wrote, and this is their language: and one might say if they were also cooked it would be permitted — why did the Rabbis say from the time of the first eating it requires pouring out; and regarding peace-offerings of yesterday and peace-offerings of the present where both are heter — there is no reasoning to say it is a Scriptural decree in a matter that is entirely heter, even in non-sacred matters even rabbinically, end of their words. And one must understand the nature of their difficulty and in what their astonishment lies — for at first glance it is so: the Rabbis and R' Tarfon dispute — R' Tarfon holds if one cooked in it at the beginning of the festival he may cook in it all the festival and every day becomes purging for its fellow, and the Sages disagree; and one must say Tosafot hold: granted if they were cooked it would be forbidden — the Sages properly dispute and he could not make vessels purging for its fellow for it would be noten ta'am bar noten ta'am and forbidden; but if noten ta'am bar noten ta'am is permitted — then certainly they would do so and cook day by day in one vessel; if so why do the Sages dispute: and per this explanation it appears proven Tosafot hold like Rashba — for if like Beit Yosef there is no difficulty here, in any case the difficulty is even per the view that noten ta'am bar noten ta'am is forbidden they could cook, for Temple vessel they establish on a Torah basis with bitul b'rov; and if one does not hold this reasoning of establishing on a Torah basis — then even per the view that noten ta'am bar noten ta'am is permitted Tosafot challenge nothing — how would he do purging every day, behold there is no hag'alah here, only ordinary cooking; and Beit Yosef wrote it helps since Temple vessel they establish on a Torah basis; but since the one who says so does not hold establishing on a Torah basis, this is not hag'alah at all and he challenges nothing; and perforce one must say Tosafot hold like Rashba — even though we do not say establishing on a Torah basis, nevertheless since heter absorbed it is hag'alah; if so he properly challenged, investigate — thus one might say at first glance: but after investigation one might say since Tosafot left this in difficulty — heaven forbid they resolve only that in truth we say as Beit Yosef's view Temple vessel they establish on a Torah basis, and the first Tanna does not hold this, and you must conclude; and see above siman 98 what is written there on Beit Yosef's difficulty on Rashba: and support from what Tosafot wrote "and one might say it is a Scriptural decree," etc. — where is this decree found in Torah; if what it commanded to pour out is when he did not cook in turn in another cooked dish which is like a kind of pouring out, but if he cooked in turn truly he does not need it; and also what they challenged — if so how would it be permitted in non-sacred matters even rabbinically — what connection does this have to that; and kodashim the Torah required pouring out to expel even any taste whatsoever after it became notar, but for this reason not to forbid noten ta'am bar noten ta'am from Scripture to make from this astonishment: therefore it appears more that Tosafot were uncertain in the Rabbis' matter in the mishnah "pouring out until time of eating" — one might explain the meaning immediately when eating of kodashim finished, even though the day still has much time, nevertheless the Torah required pouring out immediately before it would be cooked in it a second time so it not receive first taste and diminish through eating per Rambam's true view; and one might say per Tosafot's intent thus: granted if they were cooked it is forbidden — one may say as written that pouring out the Torah required is immediately so he not cook afterward peace-offerings and diminish through eating, and we do not rely on rov here; but for the one who says if they were cooked it is permitted — then it does not diminish through eating, so why did the Torah require pouring out immediately; and perforce one must say in truth he did not pour out after it became notar; and if so in any case he would cook in it many times — why did the Sages not hold every day becomes purging, and why need a Scriptural decree without relying on noten ta'am bar noten ta'am; therefore it was done immediately — for if so the Torah was stringent in kodashim to forbid noten ta'am bar noten ta'am, we would also forbid noten ta'am bar noten ta'am in non-sacred matters, investigate: and one must understand how Tosafot and Rosh resolved relying on basar b'chalav batel in the majority — behold in the mishnah it teaches pouring out and rinsing cold, the spit and grate they hag'alah in hot water — this mishnah is Rabbi's, and he holds there in Zevachim daf 97 pouring out and rinsing in cold; and Rabbi holds in the sugya a drop of milk min b'mino is not batel — if so how can the answer that therefore they hag'alah in boiling that every day becomes purging for its fellow — that itself is difficult why; and Tosafot's answer Temple vessel they establish on a Torah basis does not apply, for Rabbi holds min b'mino is not batel; and one must say since it is noten ta'am bar noten ta'am and it is weak taste as written, it is not in the category of min b'mino not batel, for we require full taste like blood of bull and blood of goat as written in many places — strained: but one may challenge what we challenge in Pesachim on Rav who said pots on Pesach should be broken to change them until after Pesach and make in them not in its species; and per the above — behold you do not extract from it, and the taste expelled is noten ta'am bar noten ta'am — it is weak taste and batel even in its species; and strained to say Rav challenges and Rav holds noten ta'am bar noten ta'am is forbidden — this is strained, for certainly Rav concedes it is weak taste and they do not dispute in reality, only he holds even weak taste forbids — if so there is difficulty; therefore it appears more Rava for his reasoning holds we follow after smell, and as they would return to cook in a chatat pot of yesterday peace-offerings of the present that they diminish it — so they intended to cook bull meat and afterward goat meat and afterward ram meat; and if so perhaps it is species in its species; and even Rabbi holds it is batel; nevertheless for noten ta'am bar noten ta'am since it is one taste the rule of Torah nullification and batel in its majority does not apply according to all, investigate: general principle for poskim who ruled noten ta'am bar noten ta'am is permitted — if so one should say like Rashba that regarding peace-offerings Temple vessel, etc., does not apply, there is no Temple vessel here, and what is done as hag'alah is that noten ta'am bar noten ta'am is permitted — if so his law is properly proven; but for those great ones who ruled noten ta'am bar noten ta'am is forbidden in cooking — one must say also in peace-offerings Temple vessel, etc.; if so there is no proof for his law, investigate: Taz brought here Bach's view to permit in kavush in every old earthenware vessel from what we say in Bava Metzia in old jugs it does not extract absorption for him; and Taz's view is that therefore it does not extract absorption — what it absorbs correspondingly expels from prior absorption, and in any case the measure will not be lacking; and this matter strains the Gemara that says since it absorbed it absorbed — per his words this is not to the statement, for since it absorbed it absorbed only what it absorbs correspondingly expels; but apart from distinguishing between oil and other liquids as Tosafot write there explicitly regarding pitch, see there — if so likewise in the other version since it absorbed it absorbed, one might say only regarding oil; also one may distinguish the body of the matter does not absorb since it is already absorbed and standing, therefore one need not deduct from him in measure; but taste in any case is absorbed — this is what the authors spoke of in every place, taste and not substance; and here we do not judge quantity but taste — this is absorption and so it is correct and clear; and what is in this siman regarding a drop that fell on the cover is not called iruy since the stream was interrupted from its place — below siman 105 see there, so I found.

yad_avraham.he: (סימן צ"ג סעיף א' בהג"ה) אם הכסוי חם והקדירה צוננת הכל שרי רק המאכל צריך קליפה אם אפשר לקלפו. ואם לאו הכל שרי לטעמי' אזיל שפסק בסי' צ"א ס"ד דבדבר הנבלל שאין שייך בו קליפה שרי וא"צ ס' נגד הקליפה וכמ"ש שם ע"ש. ונראה דס' נגד הלחלוחית שנפל מן הכסוי לקדירה מיהא בעיא וכמ"ש האו"ה הביאו הרב בד"מ. וזה שלא כ"כ משום דמסתמא איכא ס' כמ"ש שם. ומה שתמה עליו הד"מ האיך שייך ס' בחם לתוך צונן ע"ש. לק"מ דאדרבה קליפה לא שייך לפי מ"ש שם דמעט הלחלוחית שנפל לקדירה לא הוי אלא כלי שני. דטיפה א' כח חמימותה פוסק דלכך הקדירה שרי. א"כ ה"ה דאינו אוסר המאכל. דס"ל לאו"ה דכלי שני אינו מבליע ואינו אוסר כלל. וכמ"ש הג"ה סי' ק"ה ס"ג רק אם הרתיח אח"כ המאכל בעינן ס' נגד הלחלוחית שנפל דכן משמע באו"ה דמיירי בשהרתיחה ע"ש. או אפילו אם לא הרתיחה אלא שהמאכל דבר לח שנבלל צריך ס' כדין לח בלח. אבל אם לא הרתיחה וגם אינו דבר לח שאינו נבלל רק שהלחלוחית עומדת בעין כשנפל לכ"ע צריך קליפה כדי להשליך הלחלוחית בעין שיש שם באותו כדי קליפה. ולא משום הבליעה שכ"ש אינו מבליע. כנ"ל ברור בדעת האו"ה ולק"מ מה שהקשה עליו בד"מ ע"ש ודברי האו"ה ברורין: העולה מזה לדינא. בדין כסוי חם שנתנו על קדירה צוננת אם הרתיח אח"כ הקדירה או בדבר לח בעינן ס' נגד הלחלוחית שנפל לבד. לא הרתיח והמאכל אינו לח שנבלל בעי' ס' להשליך כ"ק משום הלחלוחית ולא משום הבליעה ודלא כהד"מ שר"ל משום שנבלע כ"ק. והוא תימא שהוא סתר מ"ש בכמה דוכתי דטפה א' כח חמימותה פוסק ואינו אוסר. ואפי' לפ"ד הש"ך לאסור הקדירה משום דהלחלוחית שנפרש מן הכסוי לקדירה ה"ל ערוי שאוסר מיהא כ"ק. וכמ"ש ס"ס דלעיל. מ"מ המאכל לכ"ע שרי דלדידי' ה"ל כלי שני ממש. שהרי נזחל הלחלוחית מן הכסוי ע"ג הקדירה ומשם למאכל. והרי כתב הג"ה לעיל סי' צ"ב ס"ז והבאתיו שם בסעיף ז' דה"ל כ"ש ממש ע"ש ודו"ק. אלא צ"ל כמ"ש דהקליפה היא כדי להשליך מה שיש באותו כ"ק איסור בעין. ואם נתבשל אח"כ א"צ ס' נגד הקליפה. אף לדעת הש"ך סי' צ"א ע"ש:
yad_avraham.en: (siman 93 seif 1 in the gloss) If the cover is hot and the pot cold — everything is permitted; only the food needs peeling if possible to peel; and if not everything is permitted — he follows his reasoning that he ruled siman 91 seif 4 that in a blended matter where peeling does not apply it is permitted and one does not need sixty against the peel; as written there see there. And it appears sixty against the moisture that fell from the cover onto the pot is in any case required, as Orach Chaim wrote that the Rav brought in Darchei Moshe; and this is not as Darchei Moshe wrote because presumably there is sixty, as written there. And what Darchei Moshe wondered at him — how is sixty relevant from hot into cold, see there: you must conclude on the contrary peeling does not apply — per what is written there the little moisture that fell on the pot is only like a kli sheni, for a single drop nullifies the force of its heat — therefore the pot is permitted; if so likewise it does not forbid the food, for Orach Chaim holds a kli sheni does not absorb and does not forbid at all, as the gloss wrote siman 105 seif 3; only if afterward the food boiled we require sixty against the moisture that fell, as Orach Chaim implies where it deals with after it boiled, see there; or even if it did not boil but the food is a moist matter that blends — sixty is required as the law of moist with moist; but if it did not boil and also is not a moist matter that blends, only the moisture stands in substance as when it fell — for all opinions peeling is required in order to remove the moisture in substance that is in that quantity of peel; and not because of absorption — all the more it does not absorb; as explained, clear in Orach Chaim's view; and you must conclude from what Darchei Moshe challenged see there — and Orach Chaim's words are clear: conclusion for practical law: regarding a hot cover placed on a cold pot — if afterward the pot boiled or in a moist matter we require sixty only against the moisture that fell; if it did not boil and the food is not moist that blends — sixty is required to remove the quantity of peel because of the moisture and not because of absorption, unlike Darchei Moshe who explained because a quantity of peel was absorbed; and this is astonishing, for it contradicts what is written in many places that a single drop nullifies the force of its heat and does not forbid; and even per Shach's view to forbid the pot because moisture that separated from the cover onto the pot is iruy that forbids — nevertheless a quantity of peel; and as written above end of siman. Nevertheless the food is permitted for all opinions, for per his view it is literally a kli sheni — for moisture trickled from the cover onto the pot and from there to the food; and behold the gloss wrote above siman 92 seif 7 and I brought it there in seif 7 that it is literally a kli sheni, see there, investigate; rather one must say as written that peeling is in order to remove what is in that quantity of peel of prohibition in substance; and if it was cooked afterward one does not need sixty against the peel — even per Shach's view siman 91 see there.

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (סי' צ"ג סס"א בהג"ה) ואם לא היה מאכל בקדירה. קשה לי הא אף אם יש מאכל בקדירה הקדירה מותרת ומה חידש בזה הרמ"א דאם ליכא מאכל בקדירה דהכל שרי ולומר דהכל שרי היינו אף בשניהם חמים הא בזה בודאי אסור הקדירה מחמת הלחלוחית שבכיסוי דבזה ל"ש סברת או"ה דקיל משאר עירוי דטיפה א' פוסק כח חמימותה דכיון דהקדירה הם במה יפסוק חמימותה וצ"ע:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: (siman 93 in the gloss) And if there was no food in the pot. I have difficulty: behold even if there is food in the pot the pot is permitted — so what did Rama innovate that if there is no food in the pot everything is permitted; and to say "everything is permitted" means even when both are hot — behold in that case certainly the pot is forbidden because of the moisture on the cover, for Orach Chaim's reasoning that it is lenient compared to other iruy does not apply — a single drop nullifies the force of its heat, for since they are pots in what will its heat be nullified — requires further study.

mateh_yehonatan.he: (סימן צ"ג) קדירה שבשל בה בשר לא יבשל בה חלב כו'. כתב הטור בשם הרשב"א דאם בישל ירקות בקדירה של בשר מותר לבשל בה אחר כך גבינה שכבר נתמעט בה כח שבלע הבשר ונקלש עד שאין ראוי לחול עליו שם איסור בב"ח בד"א כשבלע היתר כמו שאמרנו אפל בלע דבר איסור לעולם הוא באיסורו עד שיגעיל הראוי להגעיל וללבן הראוי ללבן ע"כ וראייתו מהש"ס דעבודת כוכבים ובזבחים וכמו דמבואר בב"י דכל יום ויום נעשה גיעול לחבירו. וכתב הב"י ומיהו מדברי תוס' פ' כ"ה משמע דלית להו הא דרשב"א שכתבו בשמעתין דדגים שעלו בקערה בסוף עבודת כוכבים דכל יום ויום נעשה גיעול לחבירו וטעמא משום דמינו ומינו בטיל ברוב מדאוריי' ובכלי מקדש אוקמי אדאוריי' וכ' הש"ך בס' נקה"כ שלו דדברי ב"י אלו אין להם שחר כלל דאף לד' התוס' ראיית הרשב"א מוכרחת דלאחר שנאסר הכלי לא שייך ביטול ברוב כלל דאל"כ למה צריך להגעיל כלל ע"ש א"ו דגם התוס' ס"ל דמהני הגעלה בכה"ג דנפלט הכל ואאמ"ו דלק"מ דוודאי לפי דברי התו' י"ל דלא מהני הגעלה בכה"ג והיינו משום דאינו מפליט כל הבלוע ואף שמפליט קצת מ"מ יוכל לחול עליו אח"כ שם האיסור על הנשאר והא דמהני גבי חטאת והיינו משום דזהו וודאי רוב הבליעה מפליט ולא נשאר בו רק מעט וא"כ כשיבלע אח"כ בקדירה מן ההיתר כמו ערך האיסור שהוציא הבלוע הנשארת בתוכ' בטיל ברוב ושפיר איכא למימר דאוקמוה אדאורייתא ע"י הגעלה זו אמנם זה דווקא בחטאת אבל בשאר אסורים דקיי"ל מין במינו צריך ס' וודאי לא מהני הגעלה בכה"ג. והנה לכאורה מוכח כדברי תוס' ודלא כרשב"א מהא דפסחים דף למ"ד אין טשין את התנור באליה ואם טש כל הפת כולה אסורה עד שיסיק את התנור ופריך אמאי אמר רב קדירות בפסח ישברו כו' ומשני כו' ע"ש. והנה דעת הרשב"א דאף דקיי"ל דבהיתירא בלע מהני הגעלה לכלי הצריך ליבון מ"מ בכלי חמץ להשתמש בו בפסח לא מהני הגעלה אף דהיתירא בלע משום דשמא עליו והלכך כשיבוא הפסח מקרי אסורא בלע וא"א כשיטת הרשב"א דהיכא שהגעילה עד שנקלש הטעם מהני שאינו יכול לחול עליו שם איסור קשה מאי פריך הגמ' על דברי הרב דלא מהני הסקה בקדרה מהא דתנור דאמרינן דמהני דילמא שאני התם דהיתירא בלע הלכך מהני היסק אבל חמץ בפסח דשמו עליו לא מהני הסקה דאף שנקלש טעמו ע"י מ"מ גבי איסור לעולם שהוא עומד באיסורי' אע"כ צ"ל כשיטת התוס' דאף דהתירא בלע לא מהני כלל קלישת הטעם דמ"מ יוכל לחול עליו שם איסור. ועוד יש ראיות דלא כרשב"א דהנה העולם מקשים האיך קאמרי התוס' במקדש אוקמי אדאורייתא דמין במינו בטיל ברוב הא בפ' דם חטאת מוקי להאי דכל יום נעשה גיעול לחבירו כרבי ור' הא ס"ל מין במינו לא בטיל כר"י וי"ל דהנה הרמב"ם ס"ל דמצות מריקה ושטיפה הוא קודם שנעשה נותר והתוס' ס"ל דמריקה ושטיפה הוא לאחר שנעשה נותר והנה לכאורה מהסוגיא דהשפוד ואסכלא מלבנן באור בסוף מס' ע"ז מוכח דלא כהרמב"ם דגרסינן התם השפוד והאסכלא מלבנן באור והתניא גבי קדשים השפוד והאסכלא מגעילן א"ל הכא אסורי' בלע הכא התירא בלע אמר רבא סוף סוף כי קפליט איסור קפליט אלא א' רבא כל יום ויום נעשה גיעול לחבירו א"ה הגעלה נמי לא לבעי קשי'. והנה לפי שיטת התוס' דמריקה היה אחר זמן אסור סוגי' דשמעתין אתיא כפשוטא דהמקשה פריך כי קפליט כו' היינו כיון דהגעלה הוא אחר זמן איסורא השתא נמי אסורא בלע מה לי גיעול דעובד כוכבים מה לי גיעול בקדשים וע"ז משני כל יום ויום נעשה גיעול לחבירו והיינו שפיר התירא בלע דפליט לי' קודם זמן אסור משא"כ לשיטת הרמב"ם דס"ל דמריקה ושטיפה הוא קודם זמן אסור א"כ ע"כ הא דפריך סוף סוף קפליט היינו משום דאינו מפליט כל הבלוע ונעשה נותר אחר זמן ואע"ג דאינו אלא טעם קלוש יוכל לחול עליו שם איסורי' ולא דמי לנ"ט בר נ"ט דהוי טעם קלוש הבא מן טעם קלוש א"כ יקשה מאי משני כל יום ויום נעשה גיעול לחבירו אכתי ק' דהא נשאר הבלוע בתוכו ונעשה נותר אחר זמן אכן לפמש"ל בשם הב"י לשיטת התוס' דהבלוע בטיל בתוך הכלי א"כ שפיר קא קשי' לי' סוף סוף איסורא קפליט היינו דבלוע בתוכו נעשה נותר אחר זמן וא"ל דנתבטל תוך הכלי הא האי הגעלה הוי ע"י מים והוי אינו מינו עם הבלוע וע"ז משני כל יום ויום נעשה גיעול לחבירו וא"כ הוי מינו עם הבלוע ושפיר איכא למימר שנתבטל עם בלוע ברובא דאוקמי אדאורייתא ופריך הגמ' אי הכי הגעלה נמי לא לבעי דאף דאינו נקלש טעמא מקמי הכי מ"מ נמי יוכל להגעיל בכה"ג דנתבטל ברוב בכל הכלי לפ"ז מתורץ נמי מה שמקשים על תוס' דכ' מקדש אוקמי אדאורייתא הא האי מתני' ר' היא דס"ל מינו במינו לא בטיל דהנה כתבו התוס' ביבמות פרק הערל דביבש ביבש מודה ר"י דבטיל וע"כ דהטעם דביבש ביבש ליכא כאן טעם איסור כלל דבשלמא לח בלח דאיכא כאן טעם איסור א"כ מיד כשקבלה ההיתר טעם משהו מן האיסור נעשה הכל איסור ושוב ליכא רוב היתר לבטלו משא"כ ביבש דליכא בהיתר טעם משהו המקבל מן האיסור א"כ ההיתר בכ"מ שהוא עומד בפ"ע ושפיר הוי כאן רוב היתר לבטלו א"כ ה"ה הכא בטעם קלוש אף שהוא איסור מ"מ אינו יוכל לבוא ע"י נתינת טעם גמור בהיתר שיתהפך בו טעם היתר לאיסור ושפיר בטיל ברוב לפ"ז לק"מ דהכא דמעיקרא היו מגעילין ברותחין א"כ נקלוש טעמא ואח"כ כשמתבשלין בה שלמים שפיר איכא ביטול ברוב אפי' לרבי משום דהוי כיבש ביבש כמ"ש ולק"מ וכ"ז לשיטת תוס' משא"כ לשיטת הרשב"א דס"ל דהא דאמרינן דכל יום ויום נעשה גיעול לחבירו לאו משום בטיל ברוב אתינא עליה רק משום דאיכא טעם קלוש ואין ראוי לחול עליו שם איסור א"כ לא אזלי כל הסוגיא בהא דפריך הגמ' ס"ס כו' דהא שפיר מהני דהא עדיין היתר הוא והטעם נקלש ושוב לא חייל עלי' שם איסור א"ו מוכח כהתוס' ודו"ק:
mateh_yehonatan.en: (siman 93) A pot in which meat was cooked — one may not cook milk in it, etc. Tur wrote in name of Rashba that if one cooked vegetables in a pot of meat it is permitted to cook cheese in it afterward, for the power of what the meat absorbed was already diminished and the taste weakened until it is not fit to impart prohibitory status in basar b'chalav; in what case — when it absorbed heter, as we said — but if it absorbed forbidden matter it is always in its forbidden state until one hag'alahs what is fit for hag'alah and libuns what is fit for libun, etc.; and his proof is from the Talmud in Avodah Zarah and Zevachim, as explained in Beit Yosef that every day becomes purging for its fellow. And Beit Yosef wrote: however from Tosafot chapter 25 it implies they do not hold this of Rashba that they wrote in the sugya regarding fish that ascended in a bowl at the end of Avodah Zarah that every day becomes purging for its fellow, and the reason is because min b'mino is batel b'rov d'oraisa and in a Temple vessel they establish it on a Torah basis. And Shach wrote in his Netivot HaKesef that Beit Yosef's words have no substance at all, for even according to Tosafot Rashba's proof is compelled — that after the vessel became forbidden bitul b'rov does not apply at all, for otherwise why would hag'alah be needed at all, see there; or also Tosafot hold hag'alah helps in such a case when everything is expelled — and I might say you must conclude that certainly according to Tosafot's words one can say hag'alah does not help in such a case, and this is because it does not expel all the absorption, and even though it expels some, nevertheless the forbidden name can impart upon what remains; and that which helps regarding chatat is because certainly the majority of the absorption is expelled and only a little remains in it, and therefore when it absorbs afterward in the pot from heter like the measure of forbidden matter that the expelled absorption that remained inside brought out — it is batel b'rov, and properly one can say they established it on a Torah basis through this hag'alah; however this is specifically regarding chatat, but for other prohibitions where we hold min b'mino requires sixty, certainly hag'alah does not help in such a case. And here it appears proven like Tosafot and not like Rashba from Pesachim daf 30 per the view that one does not plaster the oven with dough in the attic, and if he plastered all the bread is forbidden until he fires the oven — and it challenges: why did Rav say pots on Pesach should be broken, etc., and answers, etc., see there. And Rashba's view: even though we hold that if heter absorbed hag'alah helps for a vessel requiring libun, nevertheless for a chametz vessel to use on Pesach hag'alah does not help even though heter absorbed, because perhaps chametz is upon it, and therefore when Pesach arrives it is called forbidden absorption — and if so per Rashba's view that where one hag'alahs until the taste weakened it helps that forbidden status cannot impart upon it — difficult: why does the Gemara challenge Rav's words that firing does not help for a pot from the oven that we say helps; perhaps it is different there because heter absorbed therefore firing helps, but chametz on Pesach that is named upon it — firing does not help, for even though its taste weakened through hag'alah, nevertheless regarding prohibition that forever stands in its prohibitions, therefore one must say per Tosafot's view that even though heter absorbed, weakening of taste entirely does not help, nevertheless forbidden taste can impart upon it. And there are further proofs against Rashba: behold the world challenges how Tosafot say in the Temple they establish on a Torah basis that min b'mino is batel b'rov — behold in the chapter on blood of chatat they establish this that every day becomes purging for its fellow like Rabbi, and Rabbi holds min b'mino is not batel like R' Yehudah; and one might say: Rambam holds the mitzvah of pouring out and rinsing is before it becomes notar, and Tosafot hold pouring out and rinsing is after it becomes notar; and here it appears from the sugya of the spit and grate whitened in fire at the end of tractate Avodah Zarah it is not like Rambam — for we read there the spit and grate are whitened in fire, and it was taught regarding kodashim the spit and grate are hag'alah in boiling; he said to him: here forbidden matter absorbed, here heter absorbed; Rava said: in the end when it expels, forbidden matter it expels; except according to Rava every day becomes purging for its fellow — if so hag'alah too should not be required — difficult. And per Tosafot's view that pouring out was after the time of prohibition, the sugya of our mishnah accords with the straightforward challenge that challenges when it expels, etc. — meaning since hag'alah is after the time of prohibition, now too forbidden matter is absorbed — what difference to me purging of idol worship, what difference to me purging in kodashim; and on this it answers every day becomes purging for its fellow — meaning properly heter absorbed expels for him before the time of prohibition, unlike per Rambam's view who holds pouring out and rinsing is before the time of prohibition — then necessarily that which challenges in the end when it expels is because it does not expel all the absorption and it becomes notar after time, and even though it is only weak taste it can impart upon it forbidden status, and it is not comparable to noten ta'am bar noten ta'am which is weak taste from weak taste; if so one should challenge why does it answer every day becomes purging for its fellow — still difficult, for behold the absorption remained inside and became notar after time; however per what I wrote in name of Beit Yosef per Tosafot's view that absorption is batel inside the vessel — then he properly challenges him in the end forbidden matter it expels — meaning absorption inside became notar after time; and one might say it was annulled inside the vessel — behold this hag'alah is through water and it is not its species with the absorption; and on this it answers every day becomes purging for its fellow — and if so it is its species with the absorption, and properly one can say it was annulled with absorption in the majority that they establish on a Torah basis; and the Gemara challenges if so hag'alah too should not be required — for even though taste is not weakened beforehand, nevertheless one could hag'alah in such a case that it was annulled b'rov in the entire vessel; therefore it also resolves what they challenge on Tosafot who wrote in the Temple they establish on a Torah basis — behold this mishnah is Rabbi's who holds min b'mino is not batel: behold Tosafot wrote in Yevamot chapter HaAreil that in dry with dry R' Yehudah concedes it is batel, and necessarily the reason in dry with dry there is no taste of prohibition at all — for granted moist with moist where there is taste of prohibition here, when the heter received some taste from the prohibition everything became prohibition and there is no longer majority heter to annul it; unlike in dry where there is no taste in the heter receiving from the prohibition — then the heter everywhere stands by itself and properly here is majority heter to annul it; if so likewise here with weak taste — even though it is prohibition, nevertheless it cannot come through imparting full taste in heter that heter taste turns to prohibition, and properly it is batel b'rov; therefore you must conclude that here where initially they hag'alah in boiling — then taste weakens, and afterward when they cook peace-offerings in it there is properly bitul b'rov even per Rabbi because it is like dry with dry as written — and you must conclude; and all this per Tosafot's view, unlike Rashba's view who holds that what we say every day becomes purging for its fellow does not come because of bitul b'rov — we derive it only because there is weak taste and it is not fit to impart upon it forbidden status; if so the entire sugya does not follow this that the Gemara challenges in the end, etc. — for it properly helps, for it is still heter and taste weakened and forbidden status no longer applies upon it — or it is proven like Tosafot, investigate.
